title: sse: fix streaming chunking & framing for partial JSON, delimiter ordering and token-event ordering
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: Several customers reported malformed JSON when consuming server-sent-event (SSE) streaming responses in the OpenAI-compat layer and the native /v1/streams endpoint. Symptoms included early closing of partial JSON objects, duplicated or missing delimiter events, and out-of-order token vs. delimiter events when a single logical frame spans multiple low-level chunks. Root cause: the streaming runtime's chunking/framing pipeline treated delimiter events ("delimiter") and token events as independent emit paths and did not preserve the strict in-order relationship for partial-json outputs. Under load and specific batch/aggregation thresholds the flush/merge logic could reorder a delimiter event behind subsequent token events or coalesce separators into the wrong chunk boundary. This led to partial JSON fragments being emitted out-of-order and clients failing partial-json parsing. What this PR does: 1) Reorders emission paths so delimiter events are enqueued and flushed ahead of subsequent token events for partial-json streams; 2) Adds an explicit boundary marker and enforced flush when a partial JSON object closes to avoid delimiter/token reordering across flush boundaries; 3) Tightens chunk coalescing logic to avoid combining a delimiter-only chunk with trailing tokens in the same emission when partial-json mode is enabled; 4) Adds integration tests that replay previously failing traces and a regression test harness that fuzzes chunk boundaries and event ordering; 5) Updates OpenAI-compat layer docs to call out the stronger ordering guarantees and a minor client-side backcompat note. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce with unit and integration tests (replay traces from SUP-783) - [x] Fix framing and chunking logic in streaming runtime - [x] Add regression + fuzz tests - [x] Validate with e2e streaming harness and real clients (internal canary) - [x] Add release notes and OpenAI-compat docs updates Related: ENG-1421 (streaming stability), ENG-1502 (sse partial-json correctness). Link to replay traces: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1421/streaming-failure-traces Notes: the change is runtime-only and backward compatible for clients; there is a brief client-side recommendation for strictly parsing per-event boundaries included in the docs.

review_comments: Ethan Moore: Comment: Can you add a note about why coalescing previously merged delimiters with trailing tokens was safe? I want to make sure we don't regress for non-partial-json workloads. Author reply: The coalescing change is gated on partial-json mode only; non-partial paths still use the old coalescer (see chunker.py line 142).
Marisol Chen: Approve after minor nit on naming (delimiter -> chunk_delim). Author reply: Renamed variable + updated tests.
Diego Alvarez: Found a flaky test in e2e harness — observed intermittent ordering reversal on heavy load. Author reply: Added explicit flush and expanded timeout in the harness; CI e2e rerun passed.
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming partial-JSON delimiter and token-event ordering — prevents malformed partial JSON for streaming clients.
Improvement: stronger ordering guarantees documented for OpenAI-compat streaming endpoints.
Test: new regression and fuzz tests added to prevent future regressions.
notes: Rollout: rolled out to canary and then main cluster over 24 hours; no customer reports post-merge.
Monitoring: added alert for parse-error-rate on streaming endpoints; threshold tuned during canary.
Backcompat: clients that relied on prior loosening of boundaries should continue to work; document recommends strict per-event parsing for best behavior.
